params.headline: One pass in, one pass out, and a loop in the middle
params.note: Parameters are shared across every tick.

beats.intent: The recurrence sits after the encoder, not around it.
beats.narration: The encoder does the heavy lifting first, in the style SwinIR established. Then the field is cut into windows, and nothing is pooled away on the way through. The thought machine sits here in the middle, working on what the windows hold. Only at the very end does the decoder upsample, four times over. That loop is a single tick, and it runs in place rather than around the whole pipeline. Every tick reuses the same weights, so thinking for longer costs time and not memory.

params.headline: The encoder makes the field; the partition keeps it

terms.label: SwinIR-style encoder — LR in, dense feature field out
window partition — every token survives it

beats.intent: Encoding and partitioning, with nothing discarded.
beats.narration: The encoder turns the low-resolution image into a dense feature field. The partition then cuts that field into windows without throwing any of it away.

params.headline: The method is mid-pack on parameters, not the smallest
params.note: Smaller is better; DQ-CTM-SR is second largest here.

beats.intent: Where the method sits on cost.
beats.narration: On parameters the method is the second largest here, at 1.13 million. So this is not the cheap option, and the paper never claims it is.
